requirement: Where subagents are unavailable, the `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to review each group themselves against the review prompt of {cite}`requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.review_prompt`, one group at a time, before presenting any group to the user.
rationale:
The requirement is a documentation obligation on the `habeas-requirements` skill. It has four parts. When subagents are unavailable, the skill directs agents to review each group themselves. The review is against the review prompt. It goes one group at a time. It happens before any group is presented to the user.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_reviews_groups_itself_without_subagents]` is marked `{test}` for the subject. It uses `step_of` on the `habeas-requirements` skill. `step_of` panics unless some workflow step contains the exact phrase "If you can't start subagents, review each group yourself against the prompt, one group at a time". That one assertion covers the conditional (subagents unavailable), the agent reviewing it themselves, the reference to "the prompt", and the one-group-at-a-time rule.

The test then asserts that this fallback step's number is strictly less than the step number of "Present each group to the user". That covers the ordering obligation of reviewing before presenting any group.

The phrase check does not verify that "the prompt" is the review prompt. I did not treat that as a gap, because the prompt content is the subject of `requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.review_prompt`, which is cited as context. I found no other required behavior or boundary that the tests would miss.

text: Where subagents are unavailable, the `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents to review each group themselves against the review prompt of {cite}`requirements.cli.requirements_review_skill.review_prompt`, one group at a time, before presenting any group to the user.

The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST supply the review prompt that each group's reviewer follows. The prompt MUST direct the reviewer not to edit files. It MUST direct the reviewer to make mechanical changes itself in the revised text it returns, and to return design questions for the user.
